mappings.note: Translation v1 contains only the age of Joash (7 years) and a paragraph break marker. This content is missing from OSMAIN v1, which starts directly with 'In Jehus syvende år...'. The text in Translation v2 covers the full content of OSMAIN v1.
Translation v2 contains the full narrative of OSMAIN v1 (7th year, 40 years reign, mother Sibja from Beer-Sjeba).
Translation v3 matches OSMAIN v2 (Joash did right, Jojada guided him).
Translation v4 matches OSMAIN v3 (High places not removed, people sacrificed there).
Translation v5 contains the first half of Joash's command to priests (listing types of silver). OSMAIN v4 continues into v5.
Translation v6 completes the command started in v5 (priests take silver from acquaintances to repair damages). This combines the end of OSMAIN v4 and all of OSMAIN v5.
Translation v7 matches OSMAIN v6 (23rd year, priests had not repaired damages).
Translation v8 contains the first part of Joash's question and command (Why haven't you fixed it? Do not take silver from acquaintances anymore). OSMAIN v7 continues into v8.
Translation v9 completes the command (do not take silver) and records the priests' agreement. This combines the end of OSMAIN v7 and all of OSMAIN v8.
Translation v10 describes Jojada taking the chest, boring a hole, and placing it by the altar. OSMAIN v9 continues into v10.
Translation v11 describes the priests putting silver in and the scribe/priest counting it. This combines the end of OSMAIN v9 and all of OSMAIN v10.
Translation v12 describes giving silver to foremen and paying carpenters/builders. OSMAIN v11 continues into v12.
Translation v13 lists masons, stonecutters, and materials. This combines the end of OSMAIN v11 and all of OSMAIN v12.
Translation v14 matches OSMAIN v13 (No silver vessels made from this money).
Translation v15 matches OSMAIN v14 (Money given to workers to fix the house).
Translation v16 matches OSMAIN v15 (No accounting required for workers, they acted in good faith).
Translation v17 matches OSMAIN v16 (Guilt/Sin offering silver not brought to house, belongs to priests).
Translation v18 matches OSMAIN v17 (Hazael attacks Gath and turns to Jerusalem).
Translation v19 starts the list of holy things taken by Joash (Jehoshaphat, Joram, Ahaziah) but cuts off before 'and all the gold found in the treasuries'. OSMAIN v18 continues into v19.
Translation v20 completes the list of gold taken and states that Joash's history is written in the book of kings. This combines the end of OSMAIN v18 and all of OSMAIN v19.
Translation v21 describes the conspiracy and Joash being struck at Beth-Millo. OSMAIN v20 continues into v21.
Translation v22 names the murderers (Jozabad and Jehozabad), states Joash died, was buried in David's city, and Amaziah succeeded him. This combines the end of OSMAIN v20 and all of OSMAIN v21.
